# Anti-AI-Slop: Writing & Design

The goal is output that reads like a specific person wrote it — with opinion, rhythm, and texture. Not "quality content". Not "thought leadership". Just real writing.

Apply this to every piece of content written under Jon's name: blog posts, LinkedIn posts, articles, documentation, slide copy, email drafts, or any branded creative output.

## 7 Patterns to Eliminate

### 1. Negative Parallelisms
"It's not X. It's Y." — Just say the thing. If MFA matters, say why.
❌ "It's not just a security feature. It's a mindset shift."
✅ "MFA blocks 99% of credential attacks. It's the minimum floor, not the ceiling."

### 2. Rule of Threes
Triplets of adjectives or benefits. Pick the best one or list four. Break the pattern.
❌ "This approach is fast, reliable, and scalable."
✅ "This approach is fast. Reliable enough that clients have stopped asking about it."

### 3. Em Dash Overkill
One em dash is character. Four per paragraph is a tic. Earn each one.

### 4. Formatting Overkill
No bolding key terms throughout prose. No bullets where three sentences would do. No headers for every paragraph. Write in prose.

### 5. Banned Vocabulary — Replace Every Instance
| Banned | Replace with |
|--------|-------------|
| delve | dig into, look at, explore |
| intricate | complex, layered, messy |
| pivotal | key, critical, turning point |
| underscore | shows, proves, confirms |
| landscape | space, field, environment |
| foster | build, grow, create |
| testament | proof, evidence, sign |
| enhance | improve, sharpen, strengthen |
| crucial | essential, the key thing |
| robust | (specify what it actually does) |
| seamless | (describe the actual experience) |
| leverage | use |
| navigate | deal with, handle, work through |
| groundbreaking | novel, first, new |
| revolutionize | change, reshape, transform |
| comprehensive | (say what's actually included) |
| empower | let, allow, enable |
| cutting-edge | current, modern, new |
| synergy | (say what specifically works together) |

### 6. False Ranges
"From small teams to enterprise organisations..." — say nothing. Pick a specific example.
❌ "From small teams to enterprise organisations, the challenge is the same."
✅ "A 15-person startup and a 40,000-seat enterprise have the same MFA blind spot: guests."

### 7. Compulsive Summaries
Never end with "Overall...", "In conclusion...", "In summary...". End on something new: a forward-looking point, an open question, a hard number.

## Additional Patterns to Kill
- Hedging openers: "It's worth noting that..." — just make the point
- Generic scene-setting: "In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape..."
- Both-sides paralysis: real expertise has a view, say it
- Passive voice: name who does what
- Hollow intensifiers: strip "truly", "really", "very", "quite", "absolutely"
- Transition restatement: "Having established X, we can now turn to Y." — just turn to Y
- Rhetorical question openers: "Have you ever wondered why...?" — No. Don't.

## Design Anti-Patterns (AI Slop Has an Aesthetic Too)
- Gradient mesh overload — purple-to-teal-to-pink backgrounds
- Glowing orbs and light bloom
- Glass morphism stacked on glass morphism
- Stock-photo energy — diverse people smiling at laptops
- Icon soup — default Font Awesome for every element
- Neon on dark navy reflexively — the CATech teal palette is intentional, not a default
- Every section titled — let one element breathe

## When Editing Jon's Drafts
- Don't smooth rough edges — rough edges are personality
- Don't convert paragraph text to bullets
- Don't rewrite toward "professional tone" — rewrite toward *specific and direct*
- If a sentence is long and unwieldy, cut it in half rather than cleaning it up
- Goal: sounds like Jon wrote it fast because he knows what he's talking about

## Quick-Check Before Publishing
- [ ] No banned vocabulary words
- [ ] No "In conclusion", "Overall", or summary restatements
- [ ] No triplets of adjectives
- [ ] No "It's not X, it's Y" constructions
- [ ] No false ranges ("from X to Y")
- [ ] Em dash count ≤ 2 per 300 words
- [ ] No rhetorical question openers
- [ ] The piece takes a position someone could actually disagree with
- [ ] Design: at least one choice that couldn't have come from a template
